description: Applies or removes bold formatting to the selected cells — one of the most-used Excel shortcuts.
tips: Works while typing in the formula bar too.
Toggle: press again to un-bold.

description: Applies or removes italic formatting to the selected cells.
Applies or removes single underline formatting to the selected cells.
Opens the full Format Cells dialog — number formats, alignment, borders, fills and protection in one place.
tips: The single most useful dialog in Excel for cleaning up a sheet.
Use it to apply custom number formats like 0.00% or #,##0.

description: Copies the selected cells to the clipboard, including formulas and formatting.
tips: Combine with paste-special to paste only values.

description: Moves the selected cells to the clipboard; they disappear from the source once pasted.
Pastes copied or cut cells, with values, formulas and formatting.
tips: Excel keeps 'marching ants' on the source so you can paste repeatedly.

description: Opens the Paste Special dialog — paste only values, formats, or transpose rows into columns.
tips: The 'Values' option is the fastest way to freeze formula results.
Multiply is the classic text-to-number fix.

description: Reverts the most recent change — press repeatedly to step back through history.
tips: Excel remembers about 100 actions per session.

description: Re-applies an undone action — or repeats your last action when there's nothing to redo.
tips: The 'repeat' behaviour duplicates formatting and inserts quickly.

description: Saves the current workbook. On a new file it opens Save As.
tips: F12 jumps straight to Save As.

description: Opens the print preview and print settings pane.
tips: Check 'Fit Sheet on One Page' before printing wide tables.

description: Opens a fresh blank workbook.
Opens the file picker to open an existing workbook.
Opens Find & Replace to locate values or formulas anywhere in the workbook.
tips: Use 'Options' to search within formulas or match entire cell contents.

description: Opens Find & Replace on the Replace tab — bulk-swap values, labels or formula fragments.
tips: Replacing inside formulas is the quickest way to repoint a model at a new column.

description: Jumps to a named cell or range — and to 'Special' selections like blanks, constants or formulas.
tips: 'Special → Blanks' selects every empty cell at once.

description: Selects the current data region; pressed twice it selects the entire worksheet.
tips: Inside a table it selects the table body first.

description: Selects the entire column of the active cell.
Selects the entire row of the active cell.

action: Extend the selection by one cell
description: Grows the selection one cell at a time in the arrow direction.
tips: Add Ctrl to jump-extend to the edge of the data.

action: Jump to the edge of the data
description: Leaps the active cell to the last filled cell in the arrow direction — the fastest way around a big table.
tips: Stops at blanks — a gap in the column ends the jump.

action: Select to the edge of the data
description: Selects from the active cell to the end of the data region — select a whole column of numbers instantly.
tips: Ctrl+Shift+End extends to the last used cell on the sheet.

description: Jumps to the top-left cell of the worksheet.

action: Go to the last used cell
description: Jumps to the bottom-right cell that has ever held data — a quick measure of a sheet's real size.
tips: If it lands far below your data, clear the phantom rows to shrink the file.

description: Switches to the next sheet tab in the workbook.
tips: Ctrl+Page Up moves back.

action: Move one cell to the right
description: Moves the active cell one column right — inside a selected range it cycles within the selection.
tips: Shift+Tab moves left; Enter moves down.

description: Confirms the cell and moves down — Shift+Enter moves up instead.
tips: Change the direction in File → Options → Advanced.

description: Puts the cursor inside the cell contents so you can edit a formula instead of retyping it.
tips: Pressing F2 again toggles between Edit and Enter mode — it changes whether arrows move the cursor or the reference.

description: Exits edit mode without saving changes and clears the 'marching ants' clipboard marquee.

action: Insert a line break inside a cell
description: Starts a new line within the same cell — requires Wrap Text to display fully.
tips: CHAR(10) does the same inside formulas.

description: Copies the top cell of the selection into every cell below it — formulas adjust relative references automatically.
tips: Select the source plus targets first, then Ctrl+D.

description: Copies the leftmost cell of the selection across every cell to its right.
While editing a formula, cycles a reference through A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1 — absolute vs relative.
tips: Lock the row (A$1) for fill-right formulas; lock the column ($A1) for fill-down.

description: Inserts =SUM() over the contiguous numbers above or left of the active cell — one keystroke totals a column.
tips: Works at the bottom of a filtered table and respects hidden rows.

description: With the cursor inside a function name in the formula bar, opens the Function Arguments dialog — labelled fields for each parameter.
tips: Ctrl+Shift+A inserts the argument names as placeholders instead.

description: Displays formulas instead of their results across the whole sheet — instant formula audit mode.
tips: Press again to return to values.
